scenes.heading: Dysentery and typhoid: protect your family
scenes.sub: Safe water · clean hands · safe food
scenes.narration: Floods can carry dysentery and typhoid into drinking water and food. Both come from germs in human faeces, and both can be serious, especially for young children. But they can be prevented, and they can be treated. Here is how to protect your family.

scenes.heading: How they spread
steps: Floods carry them into water and food
Dirty hands and flies carry them too
scenes.narration: The germs live in the faeces of sick people, and of some people who look well. When floodwater or overflowing latrines reach wells, tanks and food, the germs get in. Dirty hands and flies carry them onto food too.

scenes.heading: Know the signs

cards.name: Typhoid
lines: A fever that lasts for days

scenes.narration: Dysentery is diarrhoea with blood in it, often with fever and stomach cramps. Typhoid starts slowly: a fever that rises over several days and does not go away, with headache, stomach pain and weakness. Without treatment, typhoid can kill.

scenes.heading: 1. Make water safe
steps: Bring it to a rolling boil
Let it cool with the lid on
scenes.narration: First, make drinking water safe. Bring the water to a rolling boil, with big bubbles, then let it cool with the lid on, and keep it in a clean, covered container. If you cannot boil it, use water treatment tablets exactly as the packet says.

scenes.heading: 2. Wash your hands with soap
times: Before eating or feeding a child
scenes.narration: Second, wash your hands with soap and clean water. Wet your hands and rub in soap. Scrub every part: palms, backs, between the fingers and under the nails. Rinse, and let them dry in the air. Do it after the toilet, after cleaning a child, before cooking, and before eating or feeding a child.

scenes.heading: 3. Make food safe
steps: Cook it well, eat it hot
scenes.narration: Third, make food safe. Cook food well and eat it while it is hot. Wash fruit with safe water and peel it. Keep food covered, away from flies. Anyone sick with diarrhoea or fever should not cook for others.

scenes.heading: 4. Keep faeces away from water
scenes.narration: Fourth, keep faeces away from water. Always use a latrine, never open ground, and keep latrines far from wells. Put children's faeces in the latrine too, and wash your hands afterwards.

scenes.heading: Sick? See a health worker
scenes.narration: If someone has diarrhoea with blood, start O R S straight away and go to a health facility. Anyone with a fever that lasts more than three days should see a health worker too. Dysentery and typhoid need the right medicine from a health worker: take all of it, even when you feel better, and never buy antibiotics without a health worker's advice. Go at once if the person is very weak or sleepy, cannot drink, or has severe stomach pain.

scenes.heading: Safe water. Clean hands. Safe food.
scenes.vaccine: Typhoid vaccine: take it where health workers offer it
scenes.narration: Where health workers offer the typhoid vaccine, take it, and keep boiling water and washing hands. Safe water, clean hands, safe food. Share this with your family.
